title: Ionic Stability, Bond Parameters and Resonance

pages.title: Why does making ions produce a stable salt?

blocks.text: Removing an electron from a gaseous metal costs energy. If ion formation alone were the story, some familiar salts would seem unfavourable. The missing contribution is the stability of the whole ionic crystal.
We then need bond parameters to describe covalent structures quantitatively: how far apart atoms sit, how strongly they are held and how their electrons are shared.

pages.transition: Write the gas-phase ion steps before considering the crystal.

pages.title: Separate the ion-formation steps

blocks.text: For a gas-phase metal, M(g)→M⁺(g)+e⁻ requires ionisation enthalpy. Electron addition X(g)+e⁻→X⁻(g) has its own electron gain enthalpy. Adding those steps does not yet describe a solid.

In a crystal, each ion interacts with many neighbours. Strong overall electrostatic stabilisation can outweigh the preceding energy costs. An ionic solid is an extended arrangement, not a collection of isolated MX molecules.

pages.transition: The crystal contribution needs a stated process and sign convention.

pages.title: State the lattice-enthalpy convention

blocks.text: Lattice dissociation enthalpy is the enthalpy required to separate one mole of an ionic solid into its gaseous ions; it is positive. The reverse lattice-formation process has the opposite, negative sign.
Smaller ionic distances and greater ionic charges generally strengthen electrostatic attraction. Always state the process before attaching a sign: dissociation and formation are reverse operations.

Separate a process from its reverse: MX(s)→M⁺(g)+X⁻(g) is lattice dissociation; M⁺(g)+X⁻(g)→MX(s) is formation. Equal magnitudes have opposite signs. Merely quoting a negative number without naming the process can hide a convention error.

pages.transition: Describe measurable distances and angles as well as energies.

pages.title: Measure bond length and angle

blocks.text: Bond length is the equilibrium distance between bonded nuclei. In a homonuclear single bond, the covalent radius is half this distance. In a polyatomic molecule, bond angle describes the angle between bond directions at an atom.
A 198 pm Cl–Cl distance gives 99 pm per covalent radius. Angles such as those in a water molecule carry shape information that a two-dimensional connectivity diagram cannot supply.

pages.transition: Breaking a gaseous bond gives a quantitative measure of its strength.

pages.title: Interpret bond enthalpy

blocks.text: Bond dissociation enthalpy is the enthalpy required to break one mole of a specified bond in gaseous species. It is positive. Bond formation in the reverse process releases the corresponding energy.

In polyatomic molecules, successive dissociations may have different values because the remaining species changes. Mean bond enthalpy averages relevant values; it is not always the exact energy of one particular bond.

pages.transition: Bond multiplicity helps connect strength with length for related bonds.

pages.title: Relate bond order to length and strength

blocks.text: In simple Lewis terms, single, double and triple bonds have bond orders 1, 2, 3. For a comparable atom pair, greater bond order generally means a shorter, stronger bond.
C–C, C=C and C≡C illustrate the trend. It is a comparison for related bonds, not a guarantee that every triple bond between arbitrary elements exceeds every other bond in strength.

pages.transition: Some measured equalities cannot be represented by one local Lewis diagram.

pages.title: See why one ozone diagram is insufficient

blocks.text: One Lewis drawing of O₃ has a single and a double O–O bond, yet the two actual bond lengths are equal. Two canonical structures place the double bond on opposite sides.

The actual molecule is a resonance hybrid with delocalised electron density. It does not jump back and forth between independently existing single-double arrangements. The oxygen nuclei keep the same connectivity.

pages.transition: A three-bond example makes the resonance averaging clearer.

pages.title: Use carbonate to understand equivalent bonds

blocks.text: CO₃²⁻ has 24 valence electrons: 4+3×6+2. Three equivalent canonical structures each place one C=O bond at a different oxygen. The real ion has three equivalent C–O bonds.
A simple resonance average gives bond order(2+1+1)/3=4/3. Fractional bond order describes delocalised bonding; it does not mean that one-third of an electron pair is a separate local bond.

For ozone’s two equivalent O–O links, the simple resonance average is(1+2)/2=1.5. The actual molecule has one delocalised electronic structure; it is not a physical mixture of a single-bond molecule and a double-bond molecule.

pages.transition: Resonance and unequal electron sharing answer different questions.

pages.title: Distinguish resonance from polarity

blocks.text: Resonance changes how electrons are represented without moving nuclei. Bond polarity instead concerns unequal attraction for a shared pair in unlike-atom bonds. H–Cl is polar because Cl attracts the pair more strongly.

Canonical structures preserve total electron number and total charge. Do not shift atoms, change connectivity or use an equilibrium arrow to suggest a resonance hybrid is a mixture of rapidly interconverting molecules.

pages.transition: Match the structural evidence with its appropriate parameter or model.

pages.title: Match each measurement to its meaning

blocks.text: Lattice enthalpy describes an ionic solid’s conversion to or from gaseous ions. Bond length and angle describe geometry; dissociation enthalpy describes bond breaking; bond order describes bonding multiplicity or delocalisation.
Equivalent observed bonds may require resonance. A useful explanation connects a measured property with its correct model and never changes atoms or total electrons to improve a drawing.

questions.question: Why is isolated ion formation not the complete energy balance for NaCl(s)?
questions.answer: Crystal formation brings substantial lattice stabilisation involving many ion–ion interactions.

questions.question: What sign has lattice dissociation enthalpy?
questions.answer: Positive: separating the solid into gaseous ions requires energy.

questions.question: Find covalent radius from a 180 pm homonuclear single bond.
Why can mean bond enthalpy differ from a specific bond dissociation?
questions.answer: Successive bond breaking changes the chemical environment; a mean averages several values.

questions.question: Why do ozone’s equal bonds challenge one Lewis diagram?
questions.answer: One local single-double drawing predicts unequal bonds; resonance represents delocalisation and equivalent observed bonds.

questions.question: Calculate simple carbonate resonance bond order.
Do resonance structures represent rapidly interconverting separate molecules?
questions.answer: No. The real structure is one delocalised resonance hybrid.
